title: Silverforge lift-and-shift migration playbook - Redwood demo
next_steps: Redwood to share tailored cost/latency spreadsheet and quantization matrix
Silverforge to provide representative prompt corpus and 2 sample endpoints for parity test
Schedule 1-week pilot window and produce baseline metrics (week of 2026-05-04)
action_items: Samira Patel - produce recommended batching + cache config for Silverforge traffic pattern (due 2026-04-27)
Alex Morgan - send security package + SOC2 snippets and KMS integration notes (due 2026-04-22)
Maya Chen - upload 3 representative prompt sets and two model responses (due 2026-04-24)
Tom Reyes - confirm whether VPC peering or Private deployment evaluation should be pursued (due 2026-04-23)
summary: Discovery + demo focused on lift-and-shift playbook for switching some endpoints from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API. Walkthrough of Console, Optimize suggestions (batching, KV cache, quantization), and tradeoffs between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Agreed next steps to run a short pilot and share cost/latency sheet.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for hopping on, we got a full house, can you see my screen?
[00:07] Maya - Silverforge (Head of ML): yup, seeing it, looks good. thanks for organizing Alex.
[00:12] Alex (Redwood AE): cool, quick intros, i'm alex, AE on the account, and samira will run through the technical bits.
[00:18] Samira (Redwood SE): hey all, hi. excited. quick agenda, lift and shift playbook, console tour, optimize suggestions, security note, then q&a and next steps.
[00:28] Tom - Silverforge (Platform Lead): sounds good. we're expecting to move three production endpoints off OpenAI and two internal ones off Together in the next quarter.
[00:36] Jules Park (Security Architect): and we'll need to validate KMS integration and audit logs before any prod cutover.
[00:42] Alex (Redwood AE): perfect, that's exactly what we planned to show. samira, can you start with parity mapping?
[00:48] Samira (Redwood SE): yeah, so first the mapping concept, when teams move from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together we look at: model family equivalence, tokenization differences, sampling defaults, and prompt scaffolding. often the largest delta is temp/presence defaults and tokenization edge cases, also longer context models need different kv cache sizing.
[01:05] Maya - Silverforge: when you say tokenization edge cases, do you hit differences in entity splitting that affect our QA output? we've seen stuff where code blocks reflow.
[01:12] Samira: yup, sometimes punctuation handling differs; we run a small corpus through both systems and capture diffs, we have heuristics to patch prompts or adjust stop sequences. we'll show an example.
[01:23] [01:30] Samira: ok pulling up the live console, this is the routes page, you can map existing endpoints to Redwood routes, create model aliases, pin versions for rollback.
[01:37] Alex (Redwood AE): one thing to call out, for Silverforge it may make sense to use route-level canaries during the migration to limit blast radius.
[01:44] Tom: what does that look like - percentage split? would that be done in the console?
[01:49] Samira: yes, console supports traffic splits, you can do 1, 5, 20% canaries, and we have automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant if latencies spike.
[01:58] [02:05] Maya: demo time, show the parity check you mentioned earlier with the prompt set.
[02:08] Samira: sure, i uploaded a 200 prompt sample earlier. running the parity job now. ok results streaming — note the top-level summary, we compute token deltas, n-gram overlap, and a small quality delta score.
[02:20] Alex: quick aside, our "Optimize" module will recommend batching and kv cache usage based on seq length distribution, that often gives the biggest cost drop.
[02:28] Tom: can you quantify? we care about tokens / call cost and latency per request, we can't drop latency beyond a threshold.
[02:34] Samira: quick numbers from a customer with similar traffic: autosuggest endpoint, median seq len 48, batching with 16 concurrency reduced cost per token by ~22% and improved 95th latency by 10ms due to GPU packing; but note that for ultra-low-latency (sub 80ms) you may choose smaller batch sizes.
[02:50] [03:00] Jules: on encryption, we need to know whether Redwood can integrate with our GCP KMS and if audit logs include per-request metadata for compliance.
[03:08] Alex: yes, we support KMS integrations and you can export audit logs to your SIEM, we also have field-level configs for redaction at the edge. i'll follow up with the security pack.
[03:18] Maya: regarding model variants, Together has a few instruction-tuned families we rely on; how close are the Redwood-verified open models?
[03:25] Samira: we publish performance profiles for each model in our catalog — for example the 'Redwood-x-7b' maps roughly to Together-instruct-7b in latency and qualitative evals; we also often recommend small post-processing changes and temperature adjustments.
[03:38] [03:45] Tom: can we run both in parallel during the pilot? route split sounds useful but we want raw comparison latency too.
[03:51] Samira: yes, you can run parallel routes and we collect per-route telemetry. the console traces token-level timing and gives a per-token cost breakdown.
[03:59] Alex: i'll add that to the pilot plan, we want both parity quality metrics and what we call unit economics (cost per 1k tokens + tail latency).
[04:08] [04:15] Maya: what's the recommended quantization path? we use float16 on our internal rigs but we need a hosted option.
[04:20] Samira: for hosted/Dedicated we support int8 and int4 variants. our Optimize tab will recommend a quant profile per model and per workload; we can also provide a checklist for accuracy regression tests when switching quant formats.
[04:34] Tom: any caveats for KV cache across millions of short chats? our current infra stores cache in redis, would Redwood do that or internal?
[04:42] Samira: we do in-node KV cache for performance, but we also have a distributed KV option that can write shared prefixes to Redis for persistence. for your use-case we probably keep it in-memory and tune TTLs to balance hit-rate.
[04:53] [05:00] Speaker 5: um, there's some noise - are these suggestions automatic or do we run an offline job?
[05:05] Samira: they start with an offline analysis, Optimize suggests configs, but you can promote those recommendations to live via the console. it's semi-automated.
[05:13] [05:20] Alex: let's switch to the pilot logistics. we propose 2-week pilot: week one baseline collection against current endpoints, week two run Redwood variants with route splits and then 48h full-run of Redwood only.
[05:31] Maya: sounds reasonable. our timeline: Q2 we want a soft cut for low-risk endpoints. budget is tight so cost wins matter.
[05:38] Samira: that's fine, we'll prioritize endpoints with the highest token volume per call for early wins.
[05:44] [05:50] Jules: compliance gating question - for Private deployment, do you still get the same Console features? we need RBAC and audit fidelity.
[05:57] Samira: yes, Private gives you the same control plane, console, and observability. RBAC integrates with your SSO via SAML/Okta and audit logs are shipped to your storage.
[06:07] Tom: and what about version pinning? we need pin-to-digest for reproducible outputs.
[06:11] Samira: you can pin to model digest or to a deployment snapshot; we support immutable model versions.
[06:17] [06:25] Alex: i want to demo the console's cost breakdown real quick, give me 10 seconds.
[06:31] Samira: here's the route-level cost graph, token breakdown, and a per-token cost waterfall showing cache hits vs raw generation. you can see the Optimize suggestion to bump batch size from 4 to 12 for this traffic profile.
[06:44] Maya: that waterfall is really helpful. shows that 40% of calls are short and dominated by per-call overhead.
[06:50] Samira: exactly, which is why we sometimes suggest request coalescing or a tiny front-door cache for very short queries.
[06:58] [07:05] Tom: how do we validate semantic parity? our legal team cares about hallucination reduction, so we need a regression test harness.
[07:12] Samira: we run a diff job that computes n-gram overlap, F1 on labelled entities, and also a set of human eval prompts if you want. we can also export the failing prompts to a spreadsheet for manual triage.
[07:24] Alex: we can include that as part of the pilot acceptance criteria.
[07:28] [07:35] Maya: any known gotchas when migrating from Anthropic's safety schema? our product filters rely on Anthropic labels.
[07:41] Samira: safety labels differ; we recommend mapping table and an additional filter layer during transition. often a simple rule-based layer keeps continuity while you retrain your safety classifier.
[07:53] [08:00] Speaker 5: slight mis-transcription there, they said "metadata".
[08:03] Alex: thanks, noted.
[08:06] Samira: switching gears to Dedicated capacity: it's great for predictable throughput. you reserve a pool of GPUs, we put your routes on those nodes. Dedicated also allows custom quant kernels if needed.
[08:18] Tom: how elastic is it? can we burst?
[08:21] Samira: there's burst capacity options, and autoscaling policies can keep a headroom buffer. cost model is reserve + burst. we'll include a sample cost calc for your traffic.
[08:31] [08:40] Maya: can we do A/B with different quant levels? like int8 vs int4 for same model?
[08:45] Samira: yes, model variants let you run int8 and int4 side-by-side and compare quality metrics. the console traces which variant served each request.
[08:53] Alex: quick Q for Jules — what are your minimum logging retention needs?
[08:57] Jules: legally we need 12 months of redacted logs, and raw logs for 90 days, plus a separate immutable audit trail for admin actions.
[09:06] Samira: we can set retention policies per-tenant, and the audit trail is separate.
[09:11] [09:20] Maya: ok show us a parity diff example, maybe a few prompts that changed.
[09:24] Samira: pulling the comparison. here's a prompt about medical triage, on Together the answer is more conservative, on our recommended open model it's slightly more verbose. we show suggested prompt tuning: add "answer concisely" and tighten the stop sequences.
[09:39] Tom: in some cases we saw token count increase after retuning, how do you manage cost tradeoff?
[09:44] Samira: we prefer a multi-objective approach; Optimize scores candidate configs by quality delta vs unit cost delta and surfaces Pareto-optimal settings.
[09:52] [10:00] Alex: let's capture acceptance criteria for pilot: parity delta < 6% on quality metric A, 95th latency within 15% of baseline, and cost per 1k tokens less than 1.05x baseline after Optimize suggestions. ok?
[10:12] Maya: that seems fair, we'll validate.
[10:16] [10:25] Speaker 5: (crosstalk)
[10:28] Jules: governance question - who has admin rights in Private? we need to ensure separation of duties.
[10:34] Samira: you control admin roles via your SSO and can set different RBAC levels.
[10:38] Tom: and about model updates, can we schedule maintenance windows for rolling model updates?
[10:43] Samira: yes, rollouts can be scheduled and you can enable automatic rollback on regression alerts.
[10:50] [11:00] Maya: are there any benchmarks comparing Together to the Redwood-hosted variants for our use-case?
[11:06] Alex: we have an internal benchmark deck and can generate a custom one for your prompt corpus.
[11:11] Samira: also we'll do a head-to-head latency and quality run as part of the pilot.
[11:17] [11:25] Tom: operational question - how do we handle secrets and prompt telemetry? we can't log full PII.
[11:31] Jules: yes, plus we need field-level redaction and token-level hashing for searchable traces.
[11:36] Samira: Redwood supports redaction rules at the SDK level and you can hash or mask fields before logs are persisted. the console shows masked traces but retains enough metadata for debugging.
[11:48] [12:00] Alex: let's sprint through a short Console demo: routing, rollouts, and the traces view.
[12:06] Samira: here's the route configuration, this route is mapped to model alias "sf-assist-v1", pinned to digest, and you can set traffic shaping and fallbacks. traces view shows a single request timeline: fetch, kv hit/miss, decode, total latency.
[12:22] Maya: can we annotate traces with our internal correlation IDs?
[12:25] Samira: yes, we accept custom headers and propagate them through the trace.
[12:30] [12:38] Tom: about the SDK, does Redwood SDK handle automatic retries and idempotency keys? our front door expects idempotency.
[12:45] Samira: SDK supports idempotency keys, retries, and client-side coalescing. we also have a proxy pattern if you want server-side aggregation.
[12:55] [13:10] Alex: quick reminder on cost: hosted is pay-as-you-go, Dedicated is reserved, Private is licensed. we can model all three against your numbers.
[13:20] Maya: budget limit makes Hosted attractive but we may need Private for certain PHI flows.
[13:26] Samira: common approach: pilot on Hosted, move PHI-sensitive endpoints to Private or Dedicated later.
[13:33] [13:40] Tom: what SLA do you provide for Dedicated?
[13:43] Alex: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency SLOs, we can share the SLA PDF.
[13:48] [13:55] Maya: can we get a templated playbook for runbook ops in case of regression?
[13:59] Samira: yes, we have runbook templates and incident playbooks aligned with the Console alerts. will include them.
[14:07] [14:15] Speaker 5: slight pause, sorry connection hiccup.
[14:18] Alex: no worries, thanks for hanging in.
[14:22] Samira: wrapping up, i'll record the Optimize recommended config and we'll email the configs as JSON + console link.
[14:30] Maya: excellent — agree to the pilot and will upload corpus.
[14:34] Alex: great, i'll send the security docs and the cost sheet. any final questions?
[14:39] Tom: timeline for the custom benchmark?
[14:42] Samira: 3 business days after we get the sample prompts.
[14:46] Jules: thanks all.
[14:48] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with next steps.
[14:52] [End of recording]
